Issued at 1221 AM EST Mon Nov 9 2026

             -----------Synoptic Overview-----------

Modified continental air has settled over the Southeast and Florida,
with a sprawling high-pressure area extending from Georgia to
northern Texas. Near- to below-normal total moisture exists across
much of the Southeast this morning. The surface high should move
little over the next 48 hours, ensuring continued subsidence early
this week.

Right now, a split-flow jet stream configuration exists over CONUS,
with a well-defined subtropical jet extending from an upper low
over the Chihuahuan Desert to North Florida. Guidance has come into
somewhat better agreement regarding upper-air pattern evolution
over the next few days, resulting in a few forecast adjustments. A
ripple of energy from this disturbance is now expected to eject
slightly earlier, arriving over Florida by late Wednesday. Moisture
is expected to increase slightly above normal as it passes.

The polar jet dominates the upper-level pattern across North
America, with relatively weak troughs over the Northeast U.S. and
Eastern Pacific. Ensemble guidance favors a largely stationary
Rossby wave pattern over the next week or so. However, substantial
amplification is anticipated as high-latitude blocking develops,
turning both the Arctic Oscillation (AO) and North Atlantic
Oscillation (NAO) negative. As a 200+ kt Pacific jet streak deepens
a trough over the E Pacific, downstream ridging is expected to
amplify across the West, with a deep trough subsequently developing
over the Eastern U.S. beginning late Wednesday.

Surface cyclogenesis is forecast by Wednesday night over the Ohio
Valley, en route to becoming a nor'easter off of the Jersey Shore
by early Friday. Its accompanying cold front will be quickly sent
southward, passing through Florida by Thursday night. Behind it,
much drier and cooler air will be advected over the state, with
PWAT values falling to 30% of normal and 925 mb temperatures
dipping to +7 deg C by Saturday.

From Sunday into Monday, the large trough over the East Coast is
expected to move slowly into the Atlantic. Upper-level convergence
behind the trough should allow high pressure to drift toward the
Appalachians by next Monday, with boundary-layer flow gradually
turning onshore and moderation commencing.

             -------Sensible Weather & Impacts-------

Today - Tuesday...

With high soil moisture and light winds, patchy dense fog may
develop this morning. Above the surface, RH values decrease,
so the fog may be shallow. We will monitor this through the
early morning hours. If you encounter fog, slow down and use your
low-beam headlights. We may see a bit of fog again early Tuesday,
but the chances look a little lower than today.

Otherwise, a mix of clouds and sunshine continues with predominantly
dry weather as we begin the work week. Pleasant temperatures
continue with coolish mornings (upper 50s-upper 60s) and warm
afternoons (low 80s).

A lingering easterly swell will produce numerous, life-threatening
rip currents at our beaches through at least today. Please stay
out of the ocean!

Wednesday - Friday...

As mentioned in the overview, a pocket of subtropical jet
stream energy is now expected to arrive a little sooner. One
consequence is an increase in shower and storm chances on Wednesday
(30-40%), mainly in the afternoon and evening. There is still
some disagreement, particularly regarding moisture return and
instability. We will need to keep an eye on this: if adequate
instability is present, moderate effective shear associated with
the subtropical jet may yield a couple of strong storms. The
more likely scenario is scattered rain and isolated general lightning
storms. Highs should reach the low 80s once more.

Expect more cloudiness on Thursday with a continued low chance of
showers. Then, a strong cold front should pass through the area 
on Thursday night. Some additional showers may accompany this 
front through early Friday, particularly south of Orlando. Expect 
slightly cooler temps reaching the upper 70s on Thursday 
afternoon. Through early Friday, widespread heavy rainfall is not 
forecast, but there is a low chance for tallies of 1/2" to 1".

Dry conditions are forecast by Friday afternoon with slowly thinning
clouds from north to south. West-northwest winds are expected to
gust from 15 to 25 mph, with cooler high temps in the upper 60s
to low 70s.

Saturday - next Monday...

A pressure gradient between the nor'easter and high pressure over
the Missouri Valley is expected to cause chilly northwesterly flow
over the peninsula from Friday night through early Sunday. This will
send the coolest air so far this fall into Central Florida. Saturday
and Sunday mornings look to be the coldest, with lows in the
